title: [Livestream 21/12/2024] The number of visitors in the UK and their average spending
prompt: The table below shows the number of visitors in the UK and their average spending from 2003 to 2008. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates information about tourism in the UK, including visitor numbers and various spending metrics over a six-year period from 2003 to 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there was an upward trend in most tourism indicators during the period shown except for the average length of stay, which experienced a slight decline towards the end of the period. Additionally, among the indicators, only the average spending per visit showed a continuous increase.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at visitor numbers and total spending, in 2003, the UK welcomed approximately 24.715 million tourists who collectively spent 11.855 billion pounds. Both figures rose steadily over the next four years, with visitor numbers reaching a peak of about 32.778 million in 2007 before falling slightly to 31.88 million in the final year. Similarly, total expenditure increased consistently throughout the period, ending at 16.323 billion pounds in 2008.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining metrics, the average spend per visit started at 475 pounds in 2003 and showed modest fluctuations in the following years, before rising more noticeably to 511 pounds in 2008. Meanwhile, the average length of stay remained stable at 8.2 nights for the first two years, then increased slightly to 8.4 nights in 2006, but subsequently declined to 7.7 nights, and remained unchanged until the end of the period.
